title: Robotics Foundations
summary: Build, code, and test real robots while learning core engineering and problem-solving skills.
whatTheyDo: Students build and program real robots using industry-standard kits. Through exciting projects and challenges, students learn engineering concepts, coding fundamentals, and teamwork — no prior experience required.

outcomes.title: Build & Engineering
outcomes.desc: Design and construct robots using real-world engineering principles.

outcomes.title: Programming Logic
outcomes.desc: Learn block-based and text coding to control robot behaviors.

outcomes.title: Problem Solving
outcomes.desc: Tackle open-ended challenges that build critical thinking.

outcomes.title: Teamwork
outcomes.desc: Collaborate, communicate, and share ideas to reach a common goal.

forParents: Robotics Foundations is designed for beginners — no prior coding or building experience is needed. Small class sizes (max 12) mean every student gets hands-on time with the equipment, and all materials are provided.
forEducators: This program aligns with NGSS engineering-design standards and can be brought to your school as a group booking; see Bring to My School for group pricing and logistics.

title: LEGO® Robotics Engineering
summary: Design and build LEGO robots and solve real-world engineering challenges.
whatTheyDo: Using LEGO Education robotics kits, students design, build, and test robots that solve a series of themed engineering challenges, building confidence with hands-on iteration.

outcomes.title: Mechanical Design
outcomes.desc: Explore gears, levers, and simple machines.

outcomes.title: Sequencing Logic
outcomes.desc: Program step-by-step robot behaviors.

outcomes.title: Iteration
outcomes.desc: Test, fail safely, and improve a design.

outcomes.title: Collaboration
outcomes.desc: Work in pairs toward a shared build goal.

forParents: A gentle, well-supported entry point to robotics for younger builders; every session is led by two instructors.
forEducators: Group bookings available for grades 2–4; equipment provided on-site or can travel to your classroom.

title: Arduino Robotics Workshop
summary: Code robots using Arduino and advanced sensors.
whatTheyDo: Students wire, program, and debug Arduino-based robots equipped with sensors, moving from guided exercises to an independent final project.

outcomes.title: Circuits
outcomes.desc: Wire sensors, motors, and microcontrollers.

outcomes.title: C++ Basics
outcomes.desc: Write and debug real Arduino code.

outcomes.title: Systems Thinking
outcomes.desc: Combine inputs and outputs into behavior.

outcomes.title: Presentation
outcomes.desc: Demo a finished project to the group.

forParents: Recommended for students with some prior coding exposure, though motivated beginners do well with instructor support.
forEducators: A strong fit for middle-school STEM electives; can be adapted to a single-day workshop format for field trips.

title: Python Programming for Kids
summary: Learn Python by making games, animations, and interactive projects in a fun, supportive environment.
whatTheyDo: Starting from the very first line of code, students build up to small text games and interactive animations using Python, with plenty of live troubleshooting support.

outcomes.title: Syntax & Logic
outcomes.desc: Variables, loops, and conditionals.

outcomes.title: Debugging
outcomes.desc: Read errors and fix them methodically.

outcomes.title: Creative Coding
outcomes.desc: Turn logic into games and animation.

outcomes.title: Confidence
outcomes.desc: Present a finished program to peers.

included: Laptops provided on-site (or bring your own)
forParents: No experience needed. Sessions run online or at RICM — select the format that works best when registering.
forEducators: Available as an after-school enrichment block; ask about bundling with a classroom visit.

title: Game Design with Minecraft
summary: Design your own Minecraft worlds and games while learning logic, storytelling, and level design.
whatTheyDo: Students use Minecraft: Education Edition to build playable levels, learning core game-design concepts like pacing, challenge, and player feedback along the way.

outcomes.title: Level Design
outcomes.desc: Pace challenge and exploration.

outcomes.title: Redstone Logic
outcomes.desc: Build simple in-game logic circuits.

outcomes.title: Storytelling
outcomes.desc: Frame a world with narrative context.

outcomes.title: Playtesting
outcomes.desc: Give and receive constructive feedback.

forParents: A supervised, education-edition environment — not the public multiplayer version of the game.
forEducators: Popular as a library or after-school enrichment offering; can run as a single extended workshop.

title: Digital Art & Animation
summary: Create digital art and animations using industry-standard tools. No experience needed!
whatTheyDo: Students learn the fundamentals of digital illustration and frame-by-frame animation, finishing with a short animated piece of their own design.

outcomes.title: Digital Drawing
outcomes.desc: Layers, brushes, and composition.

outcomes.title: Animation Basics
outcomes.desc: Timing, easing, and keyframes.

outcomes.title: Visual Storytelling
outcomes.desc: Build a short narrative arc.

outcomes.title: Critique
outcomes.desc: Share work and give feedback.

forParents: A relaxed, creative-first environment; no drawing experience required.
forEducators: Pairs well with a Create hub visit for students exploring Tales from the Hard Drive projects.

title: Electronics & Circuits
summary: Explore the basics of electronics by building circuits and interactive projects.
whatTheyDo: From a first blinking LED to a simple alarm circuit, students build up practical, hands-on electronics skills using a breadboard and real components.

outcomes.title: Circuit Reading
outcomes.desc: Understand schematics and breadboards.

outcomes.title: Component Knowledge
outcomes.desc: Resistors, LEDs, sensors, and switches.

outcomes.title: Troubleshooting
outcomes.desc: Diagnose a circuit that isn't working.

outcomes.title: Documentation
outcomes.desc: Sketch and label a finished circuit.

forParents: All components are low-voltage and battery-powered; safety is covered in the first session.
forEducators: A strong companion to a physical-science curriculum unit on circuits.

title: AR & VR Explorers
summary: Dive into augmented and virtual reality and build your own immersive experiences.
whatTheyDo: Students try both AR and VR hardware, then use beginner-friendly creation tools to build a simple interactive scene of their own.

outcomes.title: Spatial Design
outcomes.desc: Think in 3D space, not just 2D screens.

outcomes.title: Interaction Design
outcomes.desc: Trigger events from user actions.

outcomes.title: Prototyping
outcomes.desc: Build and test a rough scene quickly.

outcomes.title: Showcase
outcomes.desc: Demo a finished experience.

forParents: Headsets are sanitized between uses; sessions include regular breaks.
forEducators: On-site only due to equipment; not currently available as a school visit.

title: Typing & Tech Skills Bootcamp
summary: Boost confidence with keyboarding, digital citizenship, and essential tech skills.
whatTheyDo: Short, focused sessions build comfort with a keyboard, file basics, and safe, responsible internet use through games and guided practice.

outcomes.title: Keyboarding
outcomes.desc: Build speed and accuracy over time.

outcomes.title: File Basics
outcomes.desc: Save, find, and organize digital work.

outcomes.title: Digital Citizenship
outcomes.desc: Practice safe, kind online behavior.

outcomes.title: Confidence
outcomes.desc: Feel comfortable at a keyboard.

forParents: A great low-pressure starting point for a first-time program participant.
forEducators: Also offered as an at-school visit for whole classrooms — see Bring to My School.

title: 3D Design & Printing Workshop
summary: Design in 3D and bring your ideas to life with professional 3D printers.
whatTheyDo: Students learn parametric 3D modeling and take a project from digital design through slicing and printing on RICM's 3D printers.

outcomes.title: 3D Modeling
outcomes.desc: Build shapes in real CAD software.

outcomes.title: Design for Printing
outcomes.desc: Understand supports, tolerances, infill.

outcomes.title: Iteration
outcomes.desc: Revise a design after a test print.

outcomes.title: Presentation
outcomes.desc: Share a finished printed object.

forParents: Registration for this session has closed; join the waitlist for the next session announcement.
forEducators: On-site only due to equipment; group bookings available by request.
